newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CO-RULING PEASANTS SEEK TO OUST PM.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CO-RULING PEASANTS SEEK TO OUST PM.

text.p: Nearly a month before Poland's general elections the Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller group in the ruling leftist coalition, said on Tuesday it will seek to dismiss the prime minister over his agricultural policies.
"The PSL leadership asked the party's parliamentary club to start procedures aimed at a no-confidence vote for the Prime Minister," PSL spokesman Aleksander Bentkowski told a news conference.

But the PSL is unlikely to push through its no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz from the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) because the opposition has said it would not support the proposal.
The Peasants demanded that the government grant farmers advance payments for the 1997 grain harvest saying such a measure was necessary to stabilise grain prices.
"The lack of clear decisions in that matter by the government causes worries in the countryside," Bentkowski said.

At the last cabient meeting a week ago Cimoszewicz had refused to discuss the issue saying the cabinet first needed to see an analysis of the grain market and PSL agriculture minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski walked out in protest.
